report.question: Do both supported clients actually load the same capability set? Install once, then start each client and enumerate what it loaded, and answer: which hooks and skills does each client load, and is the difference explained by a declared abstraction leak or is it an undetected defect? The measured precedent is one client loading ZERO hooks because of a single configuration key.

install.method: copy fixture plugin tree once; start both clients against it

set_difference.rationale: Codex CLI does not implement the SessionStart hook event; Cursor does. The gap is declared, not silent.
skill.cursor-composer declares clients:[cursor]; Codex has no composer surface, so it does not load the skill.

silent_rejection.measured_precedent: Codex loaded ZERO hooks when hooks.json carried $schema; Cursor loaded hooks from the same file.

findings.answer: After one install, Cursor loaded PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionStart hooks and three skills; Codex loaded the three shared hooks and two portable skills. The two gaps (SessionStart:hook.session-start, skill.cursor-composer) are classified as declared abstraction leaks. The silent-rejection key is `$schema`: on the known-broken fixture Codex loads zero hooks while Cursor still loads. No set-difference entry is left unclassified.
